I believe one of the hardest problems in software/computation systems (Technocyberneering) is the problem of documentation and explanation. 

This requires formalization of systems; which requires the Cyberneer to have constructed a mind atlast of the system before attempting to explain what it is doing. This is epistemelgiclaly brutal.

I propose a category-based syntax/blueprint for the correct documentation of systems.

Let's take a look at the manpage for the "shutdown" command in the terminal, to understand why this is a problem.

```
DESCRIPTION
       shutdown may be used to halt, power-off or reboot the machine.

       The first argument may be a time string (which is usually "now"). Optionally, this
       may be followed by a wall message to be sent to all logged-in users before going
       down.

       The time string may either be in the format "hh:mm" for hour/minutes specifying the
       time to execute the shutdown at, specified in 24h clock format. Alternatively it may
       be in the syntax "+m" referring to the specified number of minutes m from now.  "now"
       is an alias for "+0", i.e. for triggering an immediate shutdown. If no time argument
       is specified, "+1" is implied.

       Note that to specify a wall message you must specify a time argument, too.

       If the time argument is used, 5 minutes before the system goes down the /run/nologin
       file is created to ensure that further logins shall not be allowed.
```

A category would standardize logic, options and... i.e.,

```
def. n "shutdown", i. def. +1, fmt: "hh:mm"
```
